## Introduction

- 1 The document aims to meet the general requirements of the international community to provide trust and confidence in European Digital Identity Wallet solutions including, amongst others, applicable requirements from Regulation (EU) 2024/1183.
- 2 The document is intended to support national accreditation bodies as specified in Regulation (EU) 765/2008 in applying ISO/IEC 17065 with extensions for the accreditation of Conformity Assessment Bodies (CABs) participating in the NL EUDI Wallet Certification Scheme.
- 3 The document does not repeat requirements from ISO/IEC 17065 but follows its document structure.
- 4 Additionally, the document incorporates requirements relating to the audit of management systems, as defined in ISO/IEC 17021-1 and ISO/IEC 27006-1. In addition, ETSI EN 319 403-1 will also be taken into account.

## 1 Scope {#s-1}

- 5 This document contains requirements for competence, consistent operation and impartiality of conformity assessment bodies performing evaluation and certification of European Digital Identity Wallets under Regulation (EU) 2024/2981, in addition to the requirements contained within ISO/IEC 17065 and ISO/IEC 17025, where relevant.
- 6 CAB-CB shall be accredited in accordance with ISO/IEC 17065 for the relevant certification schemes.
- 7 Additionally, in specific schemes, CAB-ITSEF shall be accredited in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025.
- 8 Both types of CABs shall be accredited by a national accreditation body appointed pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 765/2008.
- 9 Extensions to ISO/IEC 17065 specified in this document are applicable to all certification schemes, i.e., NL-TL, NL-FS, NL-CS and NL-P-P/W.
- 10 Extensions of ISO/IEC 17065 relevant to EUCC certification scheme apply to NLCS, with limitation to the general software and network device area of competence.
- 11 Extensions to ISO/IEC 17065 that refer to ETSI EN 319 403-1 are applicable only to NL-P-P/W.
- 12 Additionally, Clause 9 specifies extensions to ISO/IEC 17025 which are relevant for CAB-ITSEF and are applicable to two certification schemes, i.e., NL-FS and NL-CS

## 7 Process requirements {#s-7}

### 7.1 General requirements {#s-7-1}

57 The requirements of ISO/IEC 17065, 7.1 apply.

58 In addition, requirements of ETSI EN 319 403-1, 7.1 are adapted in the following way:

- “TSP and the trust service(s)” are replaced with “EUDI Wallet Provider and EUDI Wallet solution related services” or “PID Provider and EUDI Wallet solution related services, where relevant.

#### 7.1.1 Object of certification {#s-7-1-1}

- 59 According to CIR (EU) 2024/2981 art 3(3), the object of certification includes the following elements:
- the software components, including settings and configurations of the wallet solutions and of the electronic identification scheme under which the wallet solutions are provided;
- the hardware components and platforms on which the software components referred to in point (a) run on or rely upon for critical operations, in cases where they are provided directly or indirectly by the wallet solution and electronic identification scheme under which they are provided and when they are required to meet the desired level of assurance for those software components;
- the processes that support the provision and operation of a wallet solution, including the user onboarding process as referred to in Article 5a of Regulation (EU) 2024/1183, covering at least enrolment, electronic means management and organisation pursuant to section 2.1, 2.2, and 2.4 of Annex I to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502.

#### 7.1.2 Certification system framework {#s-7-1-2}

- 60 The certification system consists of multiple certification schemes, each covering defined aspects of the overall framework. For each object of certification, a specific certification scheme is established, including applicable product or service requirements. All schemes are based on ISO/IEC 17065 as the conformity assessment standard. The schemes are listed in Table 1.

Table 1 Certification system framework

| Object to be certified                            | Certification scheme   | Evaluation method      | Product or service requirements   | Applicant            |
|---------------------------------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------|
| Providing of the EUDI Wallet solution (Service)   | NL-TL & NL-WP          | Audit                  | NL-P-P/W-* specifications-        | EUDI Wallet Provider |
| The issuing of PIDs to Wallet end users (Service) | NL-PP                  | Audit                  | NL-P-P-* specifications           | PID Provider         |
| Wallet solution cybersecurity (Product)           | NL-CS                  | IT security evaluation | NL-CS-* - specifications          | EUDI Wallet Provider |
| Wallet solution functional (Product)              | NL-FS                  | Testing                | NL-FS-*- specifications           | EUDI Wallet Provider |

For full list of specifications – see NL-SYS-NL

#### 7.1.3 Certification hierarchy {#s-7-1-3}

- 61 Certification of the EUDI Wallet solution shall follow a certification hierarchy consisting of top-level certification supported by subsidiary scheme-level certifications granted to respective providers. The hierarchy is illustrated in Figure 1.
- 62 Individual Wallet Providers authorized to be active in the national EUDI scheme shall hold a valid top-level certificate, whereby the Supervisory Authority shall ensure that it is notified to the European Commission in accordance with Article 5d of Regulation (EU) 2024/1183.
- 63 The top-level certificate shall cover Wallet Provider Certificate (in combination with the offered Wallet Solutions), the Wallet Provider’s compliance with the admission criteria and the PID-provider Certificate. Otherwise stated, top-level certificate shall confirm the conformity of and the Digital Identity Wallets and the and the electronic

identification scheme under which they are provided (which includes certification and admission criteria).

- 64 Each actor within relevant scheme shall hold a valid certification covering the requirements applicable to its designated role. The allocation of requirements to roles is defined in the applicable certification scheme documents (NL-TL, NL-FS, NL-CS and NL-P-P/W series). Where an entity performs multiple roles, it shall hold certification for each product or service.
- 65 When performing evaluation activity towards the top-level certification, CAB-CB may rely on the scheme-level certifications as assurance information, in accordance with NL-SYS-01. Where such certifications are relied upon, CAB-CB shall verify their validity and scope and shall not re-evaluate requirements already covered by those certifications.
- 66 The top-level certification shall not be issued or maintained if their valid certification is lacking for any components included in the EUDI wallet solution (product or service).
- 67 The top-level certificate shall not be issued or maintained unless all elements of the object of certification specified in section 7.1.1 are covered by valid certificates.

#### 7.1.4 Certification scheme {#s-7-1-4}

- 68 For each element of the object of certification, CAB-CB shall operate a certification scheme consistent with a Type 5 product certification scheme or a Type 6 service certification as defined in ISO/IEC 17067 as applicable. The certification process shall include:
- II. Determination of characteristics, through testing and audit (see 7.4);
- III. Review, the information and result of the evaluation (see 7.5);
- IV. Decisions on certification, granting, maintaining, extending, reducing, suspending and withdrawing certification (see 7.6);
- V. Attestation, licensing, issuing a certificate and granting the right to use certificates and marks (see 7.7);
- VI. Surveillance, evaluation of the operation of the process and audit of the management system (see 7.9).

- 70 The requirements of ISO/IEC 17065, 7.3 apply. In addition, the following requirements apply.

- In case evaluation and certification processes under NL-FS or NL-CS are in progress, based on the Applicant declaration, CAB-CB shall determine the status if

it does not restrict starting the process under NL-PW certification scheme. CAB-CB shall record the basis for its determination.

- In case evaluation and certification processes under NL-WP or NL-PP are in progress, based on the Applicant declaration, CAB-CB shall determine the status if it does not restrict starting the process under NL-TL certification scheme. CAB-CB shall record the basis for its determination

4. o 7.7.2 CAB-CB shall issue a new certification documentation where an evaluation, including surveillance or re-evaluations, identifies changes to the object of certification. The new certification documentation shall retain the expiry date of the original certification documentation.

### 7.8 Directory of certified products / services {#s-7-8}

- 77 The requirements of ISO/IEC 17065, 7.8 apply.
- 78 In addition, the following requirements apply.
- 7.8.1 CAB-CB shall notify the Scheme Owner and Supervisory Authority of the issuance, termination (at the client's request), suspension and withdrawal of certificate.

### 7.9 Surveillance {#s-7-9}

- 79 The requirements of ISO/IEC 17065, 7.9 apply.
- 80 7.9.1 Requirements included in ETSI EN 319 403-1, 7.9 shall be adapted in the following way:
    - “TSP” is replaced with “EUDI Wallet Provider” or “PID Provider”, and “provision of their service”, where relevant.
- 81 In addition, the following requirements apply.
- 7.9.2 CAB-CB shall ensure that surveillance activities include verification that:
- a) the Certificate Holder complies with the applicable certification scheme specified in 7.1.2 and the national certification schemes;
- b) the certified object of certification continues to meet the requirements set out in 7.1.2 and in the national certification schemes;
- 7.9.3 CAB-CB shall also conduct surveillance activities based on the following information:
- a) information from national accreditation bodies, and relevant market surveillance authorities;
- b) information resulting from audits and investigations conducted by the certification body or other competent authorities;
- c) complaints and appeals.

- 7.9.4 CAB-CB may conduct special evaluations. A special evaluation may be initiated either at the request of the Certificate Holder or by CAB-CB in response to a specific issue, such as a vulnerability notification, or market surveillance authority.
- 7.9.5 The scope of a special evaluation shall be clearly defined and limited to the activities necessary to address the specific issue that triggered it.

### 7.10 Changes affecting certification {#s-7-10}

- 82 The requirements of ISO/IEC 17065, 7.10 apply.
- 83 In addition, the following requirements apply.
- 7.10.1 Requirements included in ETSI EN 319 403-1, sections 7.4.0-7.4.7 shall be adapted in the following way:
    - “TSP” is replaced with “EUDI Wallet Provider” or “PID Provider”, and provision of their service, where relevant.
- 7.10.2 CAB-CB shall perform evaluation activities following changes to the certification scheme, including:
    - a revision of the certification scheme;
    - the publication of new specifications or standards; or
    - the publication of new versions of such specifications or standards,
- 7.10.3 CAB-CB shall take appropriate actions in accordance with information provided by the Scheme Owner.
- 7.10.4 CAB-CB shall perform evaluation activities following other changes affecting the certification, including:
    - the addition of a new wallet provider or PID provider to the scheme, or the removal of an existing wallet provider or PID provider from the scheme, if applicable;
    - a change in the identity or legal status of an existing wallet provider or PID provider within the scheme, if applicable;
    - material changes to the architecture or design of the wallet solution;
    - material changes to the enrolment or identity proofing processes;
    - significant security incident;
    - a suspension or withdrawal of certification of associated components certified by the same or other accredited certification bodies (see 7.1.3 and NL-SYS-03, Section 8.11)
    - material changes to the scheme risk register.
- 7.10.5 CAB-CB shall establish, implement and maintain a process for managing changes to the object of certification and to the conditions under which certification was granted.
- 7.10.6 CAB-CB shall determine whether changes to the object of certification or to the threat environment require additional evaluation activities. A special evaluation may also be initiated at the request of the Certificate Holder.
- 7.10.7 CAB-CB shall determine and implement appropriate actions in response to such changes. These actions shall include, as applicable:

    - additional evaluation activities;
    - review of the evaluation results;
    - issuance of revised certification documentation;
    - changes to surveillance activities.
- 7.10.8 CAB-CB shall record the rationale for excluding any of these actions.

### 7.11 Termination, reduction, suspension or withdrawal of certification {#s-7-11}

- 84 The requirements from ISO/IEC 17065, 7.11 shall apply.
- 85 In addition, the following requirements apply.
- 7.11.1 If the certification requirements are not met, CAB-CB shall:
    - inform the Certificate Holder of any non-conformity and require them to take appropriate remedial actions;
    - notify relevant market surveillance authorities when the non-conformity concerns applicable Union legislation;
    - ensure that the Certificate Holder is informed of the conditions for:
- carrying out remedial actions.
- suspension of the certification and restore the certification once the non-conformity has been resolved.
- withdrawal of the certification.
- 7.11.2 CAB-CB shall suspend the certification without undue delay once it confirms that a reported security breach or compromise affects compliance with the applicable national certification scheme.
- 7.11.3 CAB-CB shall withdraw the suspended certification if the necessary corrective actions have not been completed within an appropriate timeframe.
- 7.11.4 CAB-CB shall withdraw the certification if an identified vulnerability has not have been resolved in a timely manner considering its severity and potential impact.
- 7.11.5 In addition, the following conditions shall provide as a basis for suspension or withdrawal:
    - the certification under the NL-FS, NL-CS or NL-PP/WP certification scheme is suspended or withdrawn, and no alternative certified wallet solution is available within the scheme;
    - the Scheme Owner is unable to demonstrate continued compliance with the governance requirements of NL-SYS-01 and/or NL-TL.

### 7.12 Records {#s-7-12}

- 86 The requirements of ISO/IEC 17065, 7.12 apply.
- 87 In addition, the following requirements shall apply.
- 7.12.1 Records shall be retained in accordance with NL-SYS-01, section 5.10.

### 7.13 Complaints and appeals {#s-7-13}

- 88 The requirements of ISO/IEC 17065, 7.13 apply.
- 89 In addition, the following requirements apply.
- 7.13.1 CAB-CB shall forward to the Scheme Owner any complaints or appeals that cannot be resolved for further assessment and resolution.

## 9 Additional provisions regarding accreditation requirements for CAB-ITSEF {#s-9}

98 For NL-FS and NL-CS, CAB-ITSEF shall be accredited to ISO/IEC 17025 within the scope resulting from the characteristics of the object of certification.

- 99 Additionally, the following requirements apply.
- CAB-ITSEF shall implement necessary and appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure the confidentiality of all information obtained or generated in the performance of the certification activities, including information related to intellectual property rights. These measures shall apply to all personnel and other individuals granted access to such information. Certification of the CAB-ITSEF information security management system with the scope covering its laboratory activities is considered sufficient to meet this requirement.
- Extensions of ISO/IEC 17025 relevant to EUCC certification scheme apply to NlCS, with limitation to the general software and network device area of competence.
- Managing of personnel competence applicable to NL-FS and NL-CS shall comply with ISO/IEC 19896-1.

## 10 Transition {#s-10}

- 100 In the context of an accreditation process, CAB-CB may engage, under the supervision of the NAB and the Scheme Owner, in required certification activities that should be witnessed by the NAB.
- 101 In the context of accreditation, the CAB-ITSEF may engage, under the supervision of the NAB and the Scheme Owner, engage in the required conformity testing and cybersecurity evaluation activities, which should be witnessed by the NAB.
- 102 The issuance of certificates upon successful performance of all evaluation and certification activities requires that the CAB-CB is accredited.
- 103 The Applicant and all parties involved in these activities shall be fully aware of their status and accept the risks associated with the possibility that the CAB-CB or CABITSEF may not ultimately be accredited.

## Annex A Competence requirements for the EUDI Wallet Certification {#s-a}

- 104 NOTE: All requirements are applicable to both CAB-CB and CAB-ITSEF unless otherwise stated.

### A.1 Foundational Principles {#s-a-1}

- 105 CAB-CBs shall demonstrate the capability to perform system-level certification based on heterogeneous assurance inputs, without re-certifying components. This includes:
    - Integrating external certifications, test reports, and assurance artefacts into a coherent system-level judgment,
    - Applying risk-based reasoning where assurance is partial, indirect, or inherited,
    - Ensuring traceability between system requirements and supporting evidence, regardless of origin.
- 106 This requirement IS NOT applicable to CAB-ITSEF.

### A.2 Competence framework {#s-a-2}

#### A.2.1 Interpretation of external certifications {#s-a-2-1}

- 107 CAB shall be able to:
    - Assess scope, assurance level, and applicability of third-party certifications,
    - Interpret Security Targets, Protection Profiles, and certification reports,
    - Identify limitations, assumptions, and residual risks in external evaluations.
- 108 CAB-ITSEF shall be able to evaluate Security Targets and Protection Profiles.

#### A.2.2 Composition and Assurance Integration Competence {#s-a-2-2}

##### A.2.2.1 Evidence Integration {#s-a-2-2-1}

- 109 CAB shall:
    - Combine heterogeneous assurance artefacts (certifications, test results, audit reports) into a unified assessment,
    - Ensure consistency across different assurance sources.

##### A.2.2.2 Dependencies and Trust Analysis {#s-a-2-2-2}

- 110 CAB-CB shall:
    - Identify trust dependencies between components and services,
    - Evaluate whether assumptions made in one component certification remain valid in the composed system.

##### A.2.2.3 Composition Risk Management {#s-a-2-2-3}

## 111 CAB shall: {#s-111}

- o Assess emergent risks arising from component interaction,
    - Validate that interfaces and integrations do not invalidate existing assurances.

#### A.2.3 Regulatory Mapping and Coverage Analysis {#s-a-2-3}

##### A.2.3.1 Requirement Traceability {#s-a-2-3-1}

## 112 CAB shall: {#s-112}

- o Map European Identity Wallet requirements to available assurance evidence,
    - Maintain bidirectional traceability between requirements and demonstration of conformity of components and services.

##### A.2.3.2 Gap Identification and Treatment {#s-a-2-3-2}

- 113 CAB shall:
    - Identify coverage gaps in external certifications or assurance evidence.
    - Define compensating controls, additional evidence, or targeted evaluations.

#### A.2.4 Technical Cybersecurity Competence {#s-a-2-4}

##### A.2.4.1 Evaluation of Technical Evidence {#s-a-2-4-1}

- 114 CAB shall be capable of:
    - Assessing system architecture and trust boundaries,
    - Assessing secure design and implementation practices,
    - Performing vulnerability assessments and assessing penetration test results,
    - Performing ISMS assessment.
- 115 CAB-ITSEF shall be capable of performing vulnerability assessment, devising and performing penetration tests.

##### A.2.4.2 Cryptographic and Trust Services Expertise {#s-a-2-4-2}

- 116 CAB shall:
    - Understand cryptographic mechanisms and key management,
    - Evaluate resistance to advanced attack scenarios (e.g., high attack potential),
    - Assess secure communication and identity-binding mechanisms
- 117 CAB-ITSEF shall be capable of performing evaluation of cryptographic mechanisms and key management.

#### A.2.5 Lifecycle and Supply Chain Assurance {#s-a-2-5}

##### A.2.5.1 Secure Lifecycle Assessment {#s-a-2-5-1}

- 118 CAB shall assess:
    - Development, integration, deployment, and maintenance processes,

    - Vulnerability handling, secure update and patch management mechanisms.

##### A.2.5.2 Supply Chain and Third-Party Risk {#s-a-2-5-2}

## 119 CAB shall: {#s-119}

- o Assess supplier trustworthiness and dependency risks,
    - Verify integrity of manufacturing, provisioning, and distribution processes.

#### A.2.6 ICT Services and Operational Security Assessment {#s-a-2-6}

##### A.2.6.1 Service-Level Assurance {#s-a-2-6-1}

## 120 CAB shall: {#s-120}

- o Asses the evaluation of operational environments supporting the wallet,
    - Assess identity, authentication, and trust service integration.

##### A.2.6.2 Management Systems and Compliance {#s-a-2-6-2}

- 121 CAB shall be competent in assessing:
    - Information Security Management Systems aligned with standards such as EN ISO/IEC 27001, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, CIS Critical Security Controls, relevant ETSI standards.
    - Regulatory frameworks that include NIS2 Directive.

#### A.2.7 Reporting, Traceability, and Justification {#s-a-2-7}

##### A.2.7.1 Structured Reporting {#s-a-2-7-1}

## 122 CAB shall: {#s-122}

- o Produce clear, structured, and auditable assessment reports,
    - Ensure traceability from findings to evidence and requirements.
- 123 CAB-ITSEF shall produce clear structured and traceable technical reports based on findings to evidence and requirements.

##### A.2.7.2 Justification of Certification Decisions {#s-a-2-7-2}

## 124 CAB shall: {#s-124}

- o Clearly justify how external evidence supports certification claims,
    - Explicitly document assumptions, limitations, and residual risks.

#### A.2.8 Independence, Impartiality, and Governance {#s-a-2-8}

##### A.2.8.1 Impartial Use of External Evidence {#s-a-2-8-1}

## 125 CAB shall: {#s-125}

- o Evaluate third-party evidence without undue reliance or bias,
    - Maintain independence from component developers and certifiers or evaluators, where relevant.

#### A.2.9 Stakeholder Coordination and Ecosystem Awareness {#s-a-2-9}

##### A.2.9.1 Multi-Party Coordination {#s-a-2-9-1}

- 126 CAB shall effectively interact with:
    - Wallet providers,
    - Third-party certification bodies or testing laboratories,
    - National authorities (e.g., cybersecurity certification authorities)

##### A.2.9.2 Vulnerability and Incident Handling {#s-a-2-9-2}

- 127 CAB shall:
    - Verify processes for vulnerability disclosure and remediation,
    - Ensure alignment with coordinated vulnerability disclosure practices.

#### A.2.10 Continuous Assurance and Post-Certification Activities {#s-a-2-10}

##### A.2.10.1 Ongoing Compliance {#s-a-2-10-1}

- 128 CAB-CB shall:
    - Follow defined mechanisms for surveillance, reassessment, and change management
- 129 CAB-ITSEF shall cooperate with CAB-CB in post-certification activities.

##### A.2.10.2 Residual Risk and Monitoring {#s-a-2-10-2}

- 130 CAB-CB shall:
    - Evaluate and document residual risks at EUDI Wallet level and document the result of the evaluation
    - Recommend monitoring and mitigation strategies.
- 131 This requirement IS NOT applicable to CAB-ITSEF.
